chapter: Rockwell: Los Angeles club and sessions
title: The Beverly Cavern: layout, crowd and management
summary: Rockwell describes the club, its prices, the crowd and the owner's drink hustling.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Could you describe the setup at the... this was at the Beverly Capitol? Mm-hmm. The setup there, the atmosphere, clientele, prices, the way the band was received, general atmosphere of the... of the club and so on.

It was strictly at over 21 places. Strictly cocktail, there was a little Chinese restaurant next door. Um... As you looked at the stage, the... they had a grand piano for Purnell. And he... as you looked at the... well... as you looked at the stage, he was on the right. The banjo was just in front of him, slightly to the left. And then going across the front of the stage was George Lewis, uh... Kid Howard, and Jim Robinson. Directly in the center behind the band, it was kind of... it was in a corner. You had the drummer, Joe Watkins. Right to his left, behind the piano, was, uh... uh... Val C. Papago, the slow drag. And he was... yeah, the drum was elevated and the... and uh... slow drag was elevated. You could see, uh... drags... I guess it must have been his right foot. He was just bouncing up and down, right with the rhythm, you know. He had that angelic expression, you know, and he was looking up and he would just keep hitting those notes.
Uh... what about the, um... was there any dancing?

No dancing, it was just strictly cocktails. Uh... I don't think they even had draft gear. And the prices were, uh... it was a watered down drink, maybe 90 cents. The... the waitresses hustled. It was... it... the Lewis band, the Ori band, that played there previously, and... well, they would... they... they played there quite often when the Lewis band was not in town. They had a little older crowd, and a little heavier drinking crowd. The Lewis band drew more people and packed the place, and they were more the younger set, that would try to nurse drinks.

And the management claimed that they weren't making... even though they would... had standing room only, they weren't making out, but... I didn't care for the management, uh... they... I... It was Al Dietz, I think, was the owner. Was this, um... every night at Fainter? Six nights. All of Monday night. From, uh... 9 to 2.

Was it this feeling that the... do you think, with the management, that the band wasn't really as commercial as it might be? I mean, that seems strange to say they packed the place. They packed the place.

They packed the place, and they hustled the drinks. Um... There was a young crowd, and maybe they didn't, uh... spend the money as much as, uh... as some of the older, uh... Lushes, you know, but... Yeah. Um... but it was a great... very greedy, uh... management, and...
